Title: Get all employees - positive scenario
Description: Verify that GET /api/employe returns a list of all employees
Pre-Conditions: At least one employee exists in the database
Test Steps: Send GET request to /api/employe
Verify response status is 200 OK
Verify response body is a JSON array
Verify each element contains employee fields (id, name, role, absent, totalPresent, totalAbsent, lastAttendanceDate)

Title: Get employee by valid ID - positive scenario
Description: Verify that GET /api/employe/{id} returns the employee details when a valid existing ID is provided
Pre-Conditions: An employee with ID 1 exists in the database
Test Steps: Send GET request to /api/employe/1
Verify response status is 200 OK
Verify response body contains employee details with id=1

Title: Get employee by non-existing ID - negative scenario
Description: Verify that GET /api/employe/{id} returns an empty employee object when the ID does not exist
Test Steps: Send GET request to /api/employe/9999
Verify response status is 200 OK
Verify response body contains an empty employee object (all fields null or default)

Title: Create new employee with valid data - positive scenario
Description: Verify that POST /api/employee creates a new employee when valid data is provided
Test Steps: Send POST request to /api/employee with valid employee JSON body
Verify response status is 200 OK or 201 Created
Verify employee is saved in the database with provided details

Title: Create new employee with missing required fields - negative scenario
Description: Verify that POST /api/employee handles missing required fields gracefully
Test Steps: Send POST request to /api/employee with empty or incomplete employee JSON body
Verify response status is 200 OK (since no validation is shown in code)
Verify employee is saved with null or default values

Title: Update existing employee with valid data - positive scenario
Description: Verify that PUT /api/employee/{id} updates an existing employee when valid data is provided
Test Steps: Send PUT request to /api/employee/1 with valid updated employee JSON body
Verify response status is 200 OK
Verify response body contains updated employee details
Verify database reflects updated employee data

Title: Update non-existing employee - negative scenario
Description: Verify that PUT /api/employee/{id} returns 404 Not Found when employee ID does not exist
Test Steps: Send PUT request to /api/employee/9999 with valid employee JSON body
Verify response status is 404 Not Found
Verify response body is empty

Title: Update employee with invalid data types - negative scenario
Description: Verify that PUT /api/employee/{id} handles invalid data types in request body
Test Steps: Send PUT request to /api/employee/1 with invalid data types in JSON body (e.g. absent as string)
Verify response status is 400 Bad Request or 200 OK depending on validation
Verify employee data is not corrupted

Title: Delete existing employee - positive scenario
Description: Verify that DELETE /api/employee/{id} deletes an existing employee
Test Steps: Send DELETE request to /api/employee/1
Verify response status is 200 OK or 204 No Content
Verify employee with ID 1 no longer exists in database

Title: Delete non-existing employee - negative scenario
Description: Verify that DELETE /api/employee/{id} handles deletion of non-existing employee gracefully
Test Steps: Send DELETE request to /api/employee/9999
Verify response status is 200 OK or 204 No Content
Verify no error is thrown

Title: Get all employees when no employees exist - boundary scenario
Description: Verify that GET /api/employe returns an empty list when no employees exist
Test Steps: Send GET request to /api/employe
Verify response status is 200 OK
Verify response body is an empty JSON array

Title: Create employee with maximum length name - boundary scenario
Description: Verify that POST /api/employee accepts employee with maximum allowed length for name
Test Steps: Send POST request to /api/employee with name field set to MAX_LENGTH_NAME
Verify response status is 200 OK
Verify employee is saved with the long name

Title: Update employee with null body - negative scenario
Description: Verify that PUT /api/employee/{id} handles null or empty request body gracefully
Test Steps: Send PUT request to /api/employee/1 with empty or null body
Verify response status is 400 Bad Request or 200 OK depending on validation
Verify employee data is not changed
